A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreqPolicy and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5. Corresponding content can be matched despite section reordering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation comparisons, component ablations, VLA experiments, and physical robot evaluations, with additional results and experimental details in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation, ablation, VLA, and physical robot results, including revised task-level results in Appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: The flow-matching objective, DCT-based consistency constraints, adaptive frequency weighting, and one-step generation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains the same architecture, observation encoders, and VLA integration.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Robomimic, Adroit, MetaWorld, and LIBERO coverage and three real-world tasks. The conclusion changes its stated simulation total from 58 to 53, but the experiment descriptions and task tables show no corresponding task removal.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes Falcon-DDPM and Falcon-DDiM from the Robomimic comparison, although Falcon remains discussed in related work. The remaining comparator membership, including the appendix comparison with OpenVLA-OFT, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the 3D evaluation description from 20 episodes and the top 5 episodes to 20 segments and 'top-5 trails.' These terms are not defined, while evaluation frequency and appendix settings remain unchanged. It is unclear whether the selection procedure changed or only its wording.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same six ablation configurations and results. Appendix A.2 and Figure 4 retain the same frequency analyses, and Figure 5 retains the same real-world demonstrations. No additional robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Table 1 removes the standard deviations previously reported for IMLE Policy, including changing Can from 0.98 ± 0.01 to 0.98. The three-seed evaluation descriptions and general mean-and-standard-deviation reporting practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 5 substantially revise FreqPolicy and FlowPolicy results: their reported 3D averages change from 84.2 ± 2.6 to 78.5 ± 2.6 and from 81.5 ± 3.8 to 77.2 ± 2.8, respectively. FreqPolicy loses its reported lead on Adroit and MetaWorld Medium. Table 1 also revises ActionFlow and IMLE scores; ActionFlow's Toolhang result changes from 0.51 ± 0.02 to 0.81 ± 0.09. VLA, real-world, and ablation outcomes remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the score revisions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15 retain the same flow definitions, interpolation, consistency objectives, DCT formulation, and adaptive weighting. The reordered preliminaries introduce no new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction revises its headline performance figure from 84.2% to 78.5%, and the conclusion changes the stated simulation count from 58 to 53. The main novelty claims, one-step generation contribution, and approximately fivefold VLA acceleration claim remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly discusses extending the idea to diffusion policies and explicitly acknowledges additional computation from two forward passes. This replaces the earlier future-work discussion of improved temporal modeling, quantization, and pruning with more specific applicability and computational limitations.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's promise that code will become publicly available and adds the two-forward-pass computational disclosure. Appendix architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, training budgets, and third-party implementation links remain unchanged. No actual change in code availability is established.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 revises the characterization of GR00T N1 from requiring 16 inference steps to 4. This is a limited factual revision concerning prior work; the reference list and broader positioning around frequency consistency remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract and parts of the introduction, moves the renamed Task Setting before Preliminaries, removes the Training Strategy subheading, and rewrites the limitations paragraph. It also fixes the unresolved Figure 2 reference and replaces the preprint footer with conference information.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes shorter after two comparator rows are removed. Table highlighting and some captions change, Figure 3 task labels are reformatted, and text placement is adjusted. All five figures and eight tables remain, with their overall designs largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves agreement between Table 2 averages and subgroup means and adds a concrete computational limitation. However, Table 5 retains claims of 9.4% and 2.8% gains although its revised averages imply 3.7 and 1.3 percentage points. Section 4.1 also retains a Medium-split advantage contradicted by the revised table. These inconsistencies, unexplained score revisions, and ambiguous protocol wording coexist with the improvements, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
